blocks.content: The probability of not making any Type-I errors (false positives) over n independent tests, each at level $ $, is $ (1 -)^n $. Hence, the probability, $ $, of having at least one false positive over the entire collection is simply one minus this or $$ \pi=1-\left(1-\alpha\right)^{n} $$
If we solve for the $ $ value required for each test, $$ \alpha=1-(1-\pi)^{1/n} $$
This is often called the Dunn-Šidák method. If we note that $ (1 -)^n 1 - n $, we obtain the Bonferroni method by taking $$ \alpha=\pi/n $$

Both Equations A4.3b and A4.4 are referred to as Bonferroni corrections. In the literature, $ \pi $ is the family-wide error rate (FWER), while $ \alpha $ is the comparison-wise error rate (CWER), also referred to as the point-wise significance level (PWSL).

What value of $ $ should be used for each individual test to achieve an experiment-wide false-positive rate of 0.05?
